name: Eirzunet
known_status: One of the twenty-two imprisoned gods of Universal. Able to influence worshippers through sanctioned rites, dreams, omens, miracles, cults, and the institutions that maintain the divine prisons.
manifestation: Eirzunet’s silhouette never aligns correctly with surrounding light.
deity_description: Before the rise of rail empires, skyships, and regulated portal networks across Universal, the world existed under open divine rule, where the gods were not distant symbols of worship but active sovereign predators sustained by mortal devotion. Every prayer, sacrifice, and act of faith fed them, not metaphorically but as literal transfers of essence. Civilization grew around this reality, interpreting divine consumption as sacred balance, while unknowingly reinforcing a system built on spiritual extraction. Even after centuries of advancement, that foundational truth never changed: the gods did not simply rule reality, they fed upon it.

Within this divine ecosystem exists Eirzunet, reinterpreted in Universal myth as a demi-female lesser divinity-adjacent sorceress and exiled practitioner of divine-grade thaumaturgy. Eirzunet stands at the threshold between mortal witchcraft and predatory divine hunger, neither fully goddess nor mortal, but something deliberately self-fashioned in isolation. Her domain, the island of Aeaea, is not merely a remote sanctuary but a controlled feeding ground disguised as refuge, where hospitality itself is weaponized into ritual. Travelers arrive believing they have found safety, only to step into a carefully constructed metaphysical system designed to destabilize identity and render the soul malleable.

Aeaea operates as both temple and processing ground. Guests are offered enchanted food and drink that function as preparatory rites, softening resistance and loosening the structure of the mortal spirit. Once altered, victims are reshaped through transformation magic, most often into beasts such as swine, lions, wolves, and other forms designed not as punishment alone but as functional reconfiguration. In Universal cosmology, these transformations represent the conversion of complex mortal essence into simpler, more digestible states of vitality, allowing Eirzunet to metabolize identity itself over time.

Her predation does not mirror the overwhelming consumption practiced by the High Fathers of the pantheon. Instead, Eirzunet’s hunger is intimate and prolonged. She siphons essence gradually through enchantment, emotional dependency, and magical proximity, binding particularly resilient individuals as long-term consorts or companions. Over time, these individuals become hollow reflections of themselves, sustained just enough to remain coherent while their vitality is continuously drawn away. This cycle creates a disturbing rhythm of depletion and partial restoration, as drained remnants are sometimes returned to the world altered, disoriented, and inexplicably drawn back to Aeaea as if bound by invisible hunger.

The rare herb moly, traditionally associated with Thalunesh, is reinterpreted within this mythos as a stabilizing counter-agent against divine metabolic influence, one of the few known substances capable of resisting Eirzunet’s enchantments long enough to interrupt her feeding cycles. Those who carry it can briefly retain coherence of self, disrupting transformation and resisting the emotional and magical dependencies that sustain her domain. Even so, such resistance is temporary, and often only delays the inevitable recalibration of her influence.

Eirzunet herself embodies contradiction. She is highly intelligent, aesthetically refined, and profoundly isolated, yet driven by a compulsive need to sustain herself through stolen vitality. She does not align fully with the ruling pantheon nor oppose it outright, instead existing as a liminal imitation of divine predation scaled down into personal, ritualized intimacy. As a demi-female entity, Eirzunet exists outside rigid mortal understandings of womanhood and divinity alike, embodying an intentionally incomplete and fluid femininity that shifts between maternal allure, predatory elegance, and unnerving androgyny. Her charisma and sensuality are not mere traits but structured instruments of survival, designed to maintain proximity between herself and those she feeds upon. Those who escape her island often do so carrying fragmented knowledge of divine systems, speaking in warnings about cycles of consumption and the broader hunger underlying existence itself.
public_lore: Eirzunet governs cursed shadows, twilight transformation, forbidden magic, secrecy, and survival in darkness. Her traditions offer power to those willing to become difficult to recognize, categorize, or fully illuminate.
common_worship: Invoked by curse-workers, spies, shadow-mages, night travelers, and exiles.
religious_warning: Eirzunet’s protection often erodes certainty about identity, memory, allegiance, or the boundary between concealment and corruption.
public_origin_record: No reliable mortal record explains what this being was before the age of divine rule. Temple accounts, forbidden histories, and prison records contradict one another.
